title: If You Missed Palantir in 2023, These 4 Stocks Are Spring-Loaded
creator: BWB - Business With Brian
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Brian's 'coiled spring' framework: great stocks sit flat while the business strengthens, then snap upward — illustrated by Palantir, whose first profitable quarter (Feb 13, 2023) turned $10k into ~$310k despite five 25%+ drawdowns along the way. Palantir itself is explicitly 'not a pick for today'; instead four candidates: AMZN (BUY) — AWS grew 37% to ~$42B/quarter and is sold out into 2027, but ~$220B of data-center capex crushed free cash flow; ex-Anthropic paper gains the P/E is ~31 with PEG just over 1, and institutional 'whales' trimmed 9%, so the spring is still compressing. AVGO (BUY) — custom 'tailor-made' AI chips vs Nvidia's off-the-rack, $179B non-cancellable backlog, PEG ~0.5. SNDK (BUY) — 'pantry' memory for AI workloads, sales +175% to ~$20B and expected to double again, ~7x next-year earnings. APLD (CONDITIONAL_BUY, soft flip from BUY on Oct 3) — speculative AI data-center landlord with ~$36B of ~15-year leases; back-of-napkin fair value $10-14B vs ~$7B today, DCA only. A sponsored segment for Greenland Mines runs mid-video. Calls: AMZN/AVGO/SNDK BUY, APLD CONDITIONAL_BUY.

calls.thesis: 'Coiled spring': AWS grew 37% to ~$42B/quarter, capacity sold out into 2026-27; ex-Anthropic-paper-gains P/E ~31 with PEG just over 1 — fair price for the growth. His system says buy a little (he's already maxed out from prior-employer stock so adds nothing himself).
calls.bull_case: Once new data-center capacity comes online, the spring releases — 2023 AWS re-acceleration drove ~70% gains in 18 months.
calls.bear_case: ~$220B annual capex keeps FCF near zero; whales trimmed 9% last quarter and big money hasn't returned.

calls.thesis: Custom 'tailor-made' AI chips vs Nvidia's off-the-rack; $179B in non-cancellable backlog, PEG ~0.5 — growth at a serious discount. System says buy a little; wants proof Anthropic/customers keep paying.
calls.bull_case: 2027 AI revenue guided to double to ~$115B with supply secured; customer concentration pays off.
calls.bear_case: ~$120B of backlog from one contract; $42B Anthropic financing is circular — if Anthropic can't pay, Broadcom is on the hook.

calls.thesis: 'Pantry' memory for AI workloads; sales +175% to ~$20B, expected to double again, ~7x next-year earnings — market is pricing the bust as if it's already here. DCA because of volatility.
calls.bull_case: Data-center spend on SanDisk up ~14x YoY with ~$91B of signed multi-year contracts; memory may be structurally less cyclical this cycle.
calls.bear_case: Growth was mostly price hikes on 2/3 legacy business (phones/PCs/cards); long-term contracts cover only a quarter to a third of next year's sales; big funds cut ~30%.

calls.thesis: Speculative long-distance play: AI data-center landlord with ~$36B of ~15-year leases signed; back-of-napkin ~$10-14B fair value vs ~$7B today. Easy DCA candidate for patient investors; spring releases when rent pulls ahead of the interest bill (~end 2026). Soften from his Oct 3 BUY.
calls.bull_case: Buildings come online on schedule and next leases reprice higher given power/permit scarcity.
calls.bear_case: Rent still ~$90M/year short of interest bill; ~20% short interest; 25% below the 200-day with more slide expected.
